brief_data.hq: Stockholm (US offices opening: San Francisco, New York, Boston)
brief_data.deck: Lovable, the Stockholm platform on which non-engineers build and run software, announced a $400M Series C at a $13.3B valuation on 12 August, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund, doubling the $6.6B price set in December and funding a US office push.

risks.label: CATEGORY IN FLUX
risks.detail: Anthropic, whose Claude models Lovable is built on, is building its own app builder; rivals are raising at pace and the label 'vibe coding' may not last three years.
risks.counter: Structure the designation around 'software creation' rather than a product name; a three-year seat is itself the differentiator.

risks.label: UNNAMED MARKETING OWNER
risks.detail: The CMO exists (San Francisco, per the company's own hiring) but no leadership page names them, and there is no public CFO or COO.
risks.counter: Go through Osika, who fronts every raise; ask him to bring the CMO to the first call.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Anton Osika before the United States GP to confirm the marketing owner, agree an Austin or Las Vegas announcement window, and size an Official Software Creation Partner entry against Haas's 2027 roster.

value.text: Internal applications for the commercial and operations staff: guest and hospitality management for the US rounds, freight and travel trackers, partner-activation microsites, driver and content pages, sponsor reporting dashboards. Built on Lovable in days, hosted on the enterprise tier, with the team's data staying inside its own accounts.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: A partner with tens of millions of builders and founders as customers brings a guest list of entrepreneurs, venture investors and enterprise buyers to Austin, Miami and Las Vegas, the audience Haas's B2B partners want in the suite, and a platform for co-marketing with the team's other technology partners.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: Build-your-race-app fan activations at the US rounds; founder-and-driver content around what the team built and shipped that week; a reference customer story Lovable's enterprise sales team can tell to every business that runs on tight budgets.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Software Creation Partner designation, sidepod or mirror placement, hospitality at Austin, Miami and Las Vegas, driver and team access for Lovable's channels, and naming of the team's internal-tools programme.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 12 August Lovable announced a $400M Series C at a $13.3B valuation, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, and confirmed the same day by TechCrunch and Bloomberg. The company's own release is the primary source; the run-rate figures in it are company-stated and unaudited.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: The Series B of 18 December 2025 raised $330M at $6.6B; the Series A in July 2025 was $200M at $1.8B. A company re-priced from $1.8B to $13.3B in thirteen months has a story to tell to founders, enterprise buyers and, in time, public-market investors, and a budget to tell it with.
why_now.label: Price doubled in eight months

why_now.text: Stockholm remains headquarters, but the round funds offices in San Francisco, New York and Boston and about 450 hires this year. The chief marketing officer is already based in San Francisco. A brand moving its marketing centre of gravity to America needs American reach; F1's US rounds are the most concentrated business audience in sport.
why_now.label: The US build-out

why_now.text: The Dutch and Italian GPs open the run-in after the summer break; the United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the American stages left in 2026. Teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US and activated in full for 2027.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Haas carries Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner, Haas Automation and Haas Tooling, Mphasis as a digital-services partner, Infobip for fan messaging, CommScope and Ruckus for networking, Alpinestars for kit. Nothing on the roster builds software; Official Software Creation Partner is a clean category and Mphasis, a services integrator, is a channel rather than a rival.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: Haas is the only US-owned team that has raced for a decade, with a Kannapolis base and an owner whose machine-tool business sells to the small manufacturers who are exactly the founders and operators Lovable serves. The Miami, Austin and Las Vegas rounds are its home races, and Lovable's new offices are being opened to reach the same audience.
why_team.label: The American team

why_team.text: The leanest operation on the grid has the longest list of unbuilt tools. Hospitality, logistics, partner reporting and content sites built by the people who need them, not by race engineers, is the demonstration Lovable sells to every business customer.
why_team.label: A team that will use the product

why_team.text: A mid-grid team offers a first-time sports buyer a full partner designation, on-car placement and hospitality at a fraction of a front-running team's price, with direct access to the team's leadership for a founder-led company.
why_team.label: Price and access

ruled_out.reason: The warmest path on paper (Atlassian Ventures invested in the Series B; Lovable is built on Claude, Williams' thinking partner) but Atlassian is title partner and holds the software lane; only viable as an Atlassian-endorsed co-activation, not a clean category.
Google and Android occupy AI and developer platforms; Workday, Dropbox, Freshworks and Groq crowd the software roster.
Microsoft, owner of GitHub Copilot, is a direct rival in AI-assisted software creation.
Oracle is title partner and sells its own low-code application platform.
SAP, TeamViewer and G42 hold enterprise software and AI.
ServiceNow, Cognizant and CoreWeave occupy application platforms, services and AI compute.
HP (title), IBM and DXC Technology cover software and services.
Salesforce deployed Agentforce 360 with the team in June 2026; Confluent, Dynatrace and Octave crowd the software lane.
TWG AI is the inaugural AI partner; Core Scientific holds compute.
Open but not chosen: a first-year works team prices above a first sports seat and offers no US story; Extreme Networks and JigSpace on the roster.

brief_data.bottom_line: A $400M round at $13.3B, a company-stated run rate near $600M and a US office build-out put Lovable at peak brand-investment authority. Haas is the American team with the software-creation lane open, and two US races sit inside the window.

score_cells.note: Round closed 12 Aug; Austin and Las Vegas inside the window.

brief_data.the_case_p1: Lovable confirmed on 12 August a $400M Series C at $13.3B, led by Menlo Ventures and co-led by the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, with Balderton, Kaszek, Tencent and Regent joining and Accel, CapitalG, DST and Salesforce Ventures returning. The price has doubled since the $330M Series B at $6.6B on 18 December 2025. The company says revenue run rate passed $500M in June and should reach about $600M by end-August; more than 60 million projects have been built on the platform and its apps draw over 900 million visits a month.
brief_data.the_case_p2: The money is earmarked for scale and for America: Stockholm stays headquarters while offices open in San Francisco, New York and Boston, with about 450 hires planned this year and a chief marketing officer already based in San Francisco. A brand whose customers are founders and business owners in 150 countries now needs a stage those customers watch. It has never bought sport; the first seat is the one that defines the category.

brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. A small team runs on tools its engineers never have time to build: hospitality guest lists, freight and travel trackers, partner microsites, driver-content pages. Lovable lets commercial and operations staff build them in days on the enterprise tier. At the US rounds, a build-your-race-app activation puts fans on the platform. In return: Official Software Creation Partner, sidepod or mirror placement, US-race hospitality, founder content.
brief_data.why_team_para: Haas is the American team and the leanest on the grid: Toyota Gazoo Racing as title partner, Haas Automation selling to small manufacturers, Mphasis for digital services, Infobip for fan messaging, CommScope and Ruckus for networks. No software-creation, developer-platform or AI-application partner sits on the car. The category is open at a mid-grid price, in front of the Austin, Miami and Las Vegas crowds Lovable's US offices are opening to reach.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Software Creation Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, covering the US build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in enterprise seats. Scope: sidepod or mirror placement, the team's internal-tools programme, Austin, Miami and Las Vegas hospitality, founder-and-driver content.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 12 August and a US marketing build-out follows it. The Dutch and Italian GPs open the run-in; the United States GP in October and Las Vegas in November are the American stages, and teams settle 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Osika co-founded Lovable in Stockholm in 2023 and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Fabian Hedin, Co-Founder and CTO, and the San Francisco-based CMO, not named on any leadership page. No CFO or COO is publicly named.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Anton, you have just raised $400M to take Lovable to America, and the American team has no software-creation partner. Austin is eleven weeks away. 25 minutes to see what a three-year seat at Haas would cost and return?”
